purpose: Widely-used client-side JavaScript library for DOM manipulation, AJAX, and event handling.
description: jQuery versions before 3.5.0 are affected by a documented cross-site scripting issue (CVE-2020-11022, CVE-2020-11023) in how jQuery.htmlPrefilter() handles HTML passed to methods like .html(), .append(), and .before() — untrusted HTML containing <option> or style attributes can execute injected script. Versions before 3.4.0 also carry a separate prototype-pollution issue (CVE-2019-11358) in jQuery.extend(true, ...).
common_risks: DOM-based XSS via .html()/.append() on untrusted input
misconfigurations: bundling an outdated jQuery version copied into the project years ago and never updated
passing user-controlled strings directly into .html()/.append() regardless of jQuery version
attack_patterns: Inject HTML/script via any input reflected through a vulnerable jQuery DOM-manipulation call
Pollute Object.prototype via a crafted payload passed to a vulnerable $.extend(true, ...) call, affecting application logic that reads those polluted properties
real_world_incidents: CVE-2020-11022/11023 and CVE-2019-11358 were widely tracked findings in dependency and third-party-library scans across the industry following jQuery's own disclosure and version bump.
recommended_actions: Regardless of version, never pass unsanitized user input into .html(), .append(), .prepend(), or .before() — use .text() when inserting untrusted strings.
Audit any use of $.extend(true, ...) with user-controlled objects for prototype pollution risk.

audience_guidance.student: jQuery is a very popular helper library for writing JavaScript. Old versions had bugs where feeding certain HTML into jQuery's page-building functions could let an attacker sneak in their own script — this is called cross-site scripting (XSS).
audience_guidance.developer: Upgrade to jQuery 3.5.0+, and treat .html()/.append() the same way you'd treat innerHTML — never pass untrusted input to them without sanitizing first, no matter which jQuery version you're on.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: Fingerprint the exact jQuery version from the loaded script, then look for any place user input reaches .html()/.append()/.before() — that's the concrete exploitation path, the version alone is just a lead.
audience_guidance.pentester: Confirm the jQuery version via the library file or a global `$.fn.jquery` check, then trace any DOM sinks that pass user-controlled data through vulnerable jQuery methods.
audience_guidance.security_team: Track third-party JS library versions the same way you'd track server-side dependencies — a stale bundled jQuery copy is a common, easily-missed finding in dependency audits.
